key_insight: Lower-star persistent homology on tennis player networks captures predictive structure in match outcomes, especially when combined with rankings and graph features.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that topological data analysis can serve as a practical feature source for sports prediction systems, including a topology-only fallback when conventional ranking data are missing.
method: Build player competitive networks from ATP singles matches and apply lower-star filtration.
Extract persistent homology summaries with VAB, HNAV, HWNAV, and OW-HNPV, then analyze them with Modified Band Depth.
Train Random Forest and a modified Katz similarity model using topological, graph-theoretic, temporal, and ranking features.
evidence_signal: On about 66k matches from 2000-2025, the Random Forest reached 66.2% accuracy with AUC 0.719, while the topology-only model still achieved 63.56% accuracy and the Katz approach reached 62.48%.
watch_item: The topology pipeline relies on graph approximations and feature engineering choices, so performance and interpretability may vary with network construction, temporal weighting, and the availability of ranking data.
paper_title: Topological Data Analysis and Graph-Theoretic Approaches for Tennis Match Prediction
